zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray
zones.notes: Plants, beds, and shrubs within 4 ft of siding. Brush/roll: edge_only (drop cloth). Spray: full_cover (tarp over plantings + spray shield).
Extended overspray reach zone beyond 4 ft. Only needed for airless spray — overspray drift can travel 10-15 ft.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray
zones.notes: Adjacent walkways. Brush/roll: drop cloth runners. Spray: full tarp coverage.

zones.upgrade_scenario: Upgrades to full_cover when application_method = spray
zones.notes: Adjacent patio surfaces. Protection level driven by proximity and application method.
Exterior light fixtures mounted on or adjacent to siding. Bag or tape over fixture.
HVAC condenser units adjacent to siding. Full tarp cover during spray operations.

protection_zones_analysis.cross_spec_protection_note: Window and door protection during siding work is NOT this spec's responsibility. Window/door masking (glass, hardware, full unit cover) belongs in the respective window or door spec. If windows/doors are not being painted, their protection is scoped under the window/door spec or a separate protection mobilization. This prevents double-counting and ensures protection responsibility is clear per surface owner.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Soffit underside at eave. Often different color (white/light). Siding terminates at soffit/frieze junction. Separate scope — not included in siding spec.

Frieze board — horizontal trim board at the junction between siding and soffit/eave. Sometimes between siding and foundation. Often painted a different (trim) color. Not on every project. Separate trim scope.
Corner boards frame siding field. Often different color (accent trim). Siding field terminates at corner board — no blend/cut-in needed.
Window casing trim around openings. Siding terminates at casing. No cut-in — trim is a separate spec. Window/door protection responsibility belongs to window/door spec.
Door casing trim. Same as window casing relationship. Door protection is the door spec's responsibility.
Foundation below siding (or below frieze board if present). Not painted. Drop cloth protection at grade level.

adjacency_analysis.key_finding: Siding field has NO edge work requirements. All adjacent surfaces are separate specs (soffit, trim, foundation) or not in scope. Protection relationships only. Siding terminates at trim boards — no wet-edge blending across specs. Window/door protection is cross-spec responsibility owned by window/door specs, not siding spec.

affected_conditions.notes: Access type drives a HEIGHT MODIFIER on tasks (like FAC_HEIGHT for interior ceiling height), NOT a site condition. Applied per elevation based on working height. A project may have ground access on one elevation and scaffold on another.

excluded_conditions.rationale: Environmental conditions (wind, dew point, sun exposure, surface temperature) are important to the painting PROCESS but are NOT estimatable. They are unpredictable, change daily, and cannot be set as fixed conditions for an estimate. Including them adds estimation complexity with no practical benefit. They belong in SOP procedure notes and job-site decision protocols, not in production rate modifiers.

excluded.reason: Unpredictable. Changes hourly. Cannot set a fixed modifier for estimate.
Varies by time of day, sun angle, and season. Not predictable at bid time.
Weather-dependent. Not predictable at bid time.
Varies by elevation and season. Professional painters 'follow the shade' — this is scheduling, not estimation.

exterior_substrate_states.description: New, uncoated wood siding. May have mill glaze requiring sanding.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Sand 80-120 grit to remove mill glaze. Back-prime rear face. End-seal all cut edges. Spot-prime knots with shellac/oil-based.
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Primary NC state. Mill glaze on new lumber prevents primer adhesion — must be sanded off. Tannin-rich species (cedar, redwood) require tannin-blocking primer.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Factory-primed wood siding. Factory prime is transit protection only — NOT a field prime substitute.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Light sand for adhesion. Spot-prime any damaged/bare areas. Full field prime still required over factory prime.
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Factory primer is often thin and weather-damaged during transit/storage. Field prime is mandatory for warranty and performance. Per Exterior_Substrates_Doctrine.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Previously painted wood siding with coating intact and well-adhered.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Power wash to clean. Light sand for adhesion. Spot-prime any bare/thin areas.
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Repaint scenario. Existing coating provides base — skip full prime if adhesion test passes. Spot prime bare areas only.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Previously painted siding with chalky but adhered coating surface.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: TSP wash or power wash to remove chalk residue. Chalk rub test to verify removal. Prime with bonding primer.
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Chalk must be completely removed or bonding primer will not adhere. Common on aged latex exterior paint.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Previously painted siding with cracking, checking, or localized peeling.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Scrape loose paint. Feather edges. Sand. Spot prime bare areas. May require full prime depending on extent.
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Prep time varies dramatically based on failure extent. 10-30% failure can be scraped and spot-primed. >30% may require full strip.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Active peeling paint — widespread adhesion failure.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Heavy scraping. May require heat gun or chemical stripper. Sand to sound substrate. Full prime required.
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Most labor-intensive prep state. Prep scope unpredictable — escalates to hourly billing at QT4+. Per Exterior_Substrates_Doctrine.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Uncoated wood that has grayed and oxidized from UV/weather exposure.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Wood brightener or oxalic acid wash. Sand to remove gray surface fibers. Full prime required.
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Weathered wood has degraded surface fibers that must be removed before coating. Not the same as bare wood — surface is compromised.

exterior_substrate_states.description: Previously coated with solid body stain.
exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Power wash to clean. Sand for adhesion. Compatible topcoat required (stain or paint over stain).
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Solid stain behaves like paint for adhesion. Can be overcoated with paint if properly prepped and primed. Must verify stain type (oil vs latex) for compatibility.

exterior_substrate_states.prep_requirements: Power wash. Cannot paint directly over semi-transparent stain without bonding primer. Stain penetrates wood — creates adhesion challenge for film-forming coatings.
exterior_substrate_states.notes: Requires bonding primer before paint application. Some projects may choose to re-stain instead of painting. Verify client intent.

exterior_access_type_analysis.treatment: Modifier on tasks, not a site condition. Same concept as FAC_HEIGHT for interior.

scenarios.notes: Single-story siding, first 8 ft. No ladder needed. Baseline rate.
Two-story siding, gable ends, areas above 8 ft. Constant repositioning. Safety overhead.
Large continuous areas above 8 ft. Setup/teardown amortized. Better than ladder for runs >50 LF.
Boom/scissor lift for 3+ story or difficult access. Requires firm ground. Rental cost.

lap_horizontal_spray.notes: Airless spray, smooth lap siding. Higher end for long uninterrupted runs.

lap_horizontal_brush_roll.notes: Brush for edges/transitions, roller for field.

board_and_batten_spray.notes: Vertical profiles require multiple passes. Effective area ≈ 1.20x net area.

board_and_batten_brush_roll.notes: Brush dominant — battens require individual attention.

shingle_spray.notes: Complex profile, many edges. Backroll essential for coverage.

shingle_brush_roll.notes: Extremely labor-intensive. Each shingle edge requires brush attention.

back_prime.notes: Brush/roll on rear face. Done on ground.

power_wash.notes: For repaint prep. Pressure washer on siding.

scrape_loose_paint.notes: Hand scraping failing/peeling paint. Highly variable.

key_decisions.decision: Combined (full phase_scope). Prime and finish phases have unique task keys within the single spec.
key_decisions.rationale: NC wood siding is a single-mobilization scope — same crew primes and paints. Each phase (prime, finish) has its own task IDs and module IDs for independent rate tracking and phase-level reporting.

key_decisions.decision: Include siding_profile dimension: lap_horizontal, board_and_batten, shingle
key_decisions.rationale: Production rates vary dramatically by profile (lap spray 200 SF/hr vs shingle brush 40 SF/hr). Profile affects coverage rates, application method constraints, and modifier stacking.

key_decisions.decision: Include in prep module as conditional tasks (SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD only).
key_decisions.rationale: Back-priming and end-sealing are MANDATORY for warranty compliance and moisture management on new bare wood siding. Per Exterior_Wood_Siding_Systems_Doctrine.

key_decisions.decision: NOT this spec's responsibility. Window/door protection belongs in window/door specs.
key_decisions.rationale: If windows are being painted, the window spec covers glass masking. If windows are NOT being painted, window protection is scoped under the window spec or a separate protection mobilization. This prevents double-counting protection and creates clear ownership per surface.

key_decisions.decision: EXCLUDED from estimation modifiers. Wind, dew point, sun exposure, surface temperature are not estimatable.
key_decisions.rationale: Environmental conditions are unpredictable at bid time and change daily/hourly. They are critical to the painting PROCESS (SOP procedures, job-site decisions) but do NOT belong in production rate modifiers. Including them adds estimation complexity with no practical benefit.

key_decisions.decision: Treated as a HEIGHT MODIFIER (like FAC_HEIGHT for interior), not a site condition.
key_decisions.rationale: Access type drives a rate multiplier on tasks at elevation — conceptually identical to ceiling height modifiers for interior. It is estimatable and predictable from the project scope.

key_decisions.decision: Include all relevant exterior wood substrate states (bare, factory-primed, sound paint, chalking, failing, peeling, weathered, solid stain, semi stain).
key_decisions.rationale: While the spec is primarily NC, wood siding may arrive pre-primed. Additionally, this spec should handle the full range of existing conditions for repaint scenarios on wood siding. Prep module uses conditional tasks driven by substrate state.

key_decisions.decision: 1 prime + 2 finish coats standard at all tiers.
key_decisions.rationale: Exterior coatings rely on film build from 2 proper coats. QT5 exterior means higher scrutiny/inspection, not more coats.

research_corrections.original_claim: Window glass and door glass are protection zones for siding spec
research_corrections.corrected_to: Window/door protection belongs in window/door specs, not siding spec. If windows/doors are being painted, glass masking is that spec's responsibility. If they're NOT being painted, their protection is scoped under their own spec or separate protection mobilization.

research_corrections.original_claim: Fascia is adjacent to siding field
research_corrections.corrected_to: Fascia is part of the soffit system. Soffit is adjacent to siding at the eave. Frieze board (horizontal trim between siding and soffit/foundation) is the correct adjacency at the upper and lower siding boundaries.

research_corrections.original_claim: Wind condition, surface temperature, dew point risk, and sun exposure should be site condition modifiers with FAC_EXT_* multipliers
research_corrections.corrected_to: Environmental conditions are NOT estimatable. They are unpredictable at bid time and belong in SOP/process documentation, not production rate modifiers. Removed from spec entirely.

research_corrections.original_claim: Access type is a site condition
research_corrections.corrected_to: Access type is a HEIGHT MODIFIER (like FAC_HEIGHT for interior), not a site condition. Applied per elevation based on working height.

research_corrections.original_claim: Only SS_EXT_BARE_WOOD as substrate state for NC spec
research_corrections.corrected_to: Include all relevant exterior wood substrate states: bare, factory-primed, sound paint, chalking, failing, peeling, weathered, solid stain, semi stain. NC wood may arrive pre-primed, and spec should handle repaint scenarios.
